[2.3.76] Having rotated both hands and kissed the fingers, one should place them upon the secret place. [2.3.77]
One should worship with the previously mentioned five offerings, mudrās, and mantras, as well as with the expansions of external worship.
Having taken up the vajra and bell with the previously mentioned mudrā and mantra, one should brandish the vajra and recite this verse: "The vajra is resplendent! (sohaï vajram ullālu).
May they cross over; may the seven liberations and the purpose of the liberation through Dharma be accomplished;
may you all maintain your composure.
Having thus taken up the vajra-bell, having linked the two little fingers and joined them back-to-back, and having raised the two index fingers, one recites:

*oṃ vajraghaṇṭe raṇitapraraṇite sarvabuddhapracalite prajñāpāramitānādasvabhāve sarvahṛdayāvatoṣiṇi hūṃ 3 ho 3 svāhā* [3.1.35]. Then, while ringing the bell, one proceeds in the manner of a song consisting of the syllable *hūṃ*.
O Vajra-hu-sura,
you are capable of seeing with the eyes;
the syllable is the very nature of existence.
O you who delight in the void!
[2.3.108] Having abandoned both existence and non-existence!
O you who are known through noble wisdom!
Having broken the syllables of the being,
the remainder is reflected upon;
it is the life-force of the embrace of the two drops.
The water is made turbid; the Dharma is difficult to obtain; liberation is difficult to attain. [2.3.110]
O Yoginī, you who are all-pervasive by nature, this world has deluded me; liberation remains unaccomplished.
[2.3.111] Even a drunken dancer,
when she perceives the truth,
becomes a yoginī.
O Mother, having assumed many forms,
you have purified the seven elements;
O Vajra, you are the remover of all defects.
The Dharma leads to liberation; the true Dharma does not endure within saṃsāra; the yoginī attains liberation. o || [2.3.113]
Homage be to you, Lord of Yoga, liberator of beings! Homage be to you, the Son of All, through your singular nature! Homage be to you, the cutter of the delusion of the ocean of saṃsāra!
Homage! O you who are the singular reality, I always bow down to you.

Thereafter, having placed before him the offering vessel (*balibhāṇḍa*) containing all kinds of edible foods, along with raw fish and meat, together with the five hooks (*pañcāṅkuśa*) and nectar (*amṛta*), and having touched it with the hand holding the vajra, one should consecrate it for each of all the goddesses individually with their root mantra (*mūlamantra*) and the *sāntika* mantra, reciting it two hundred times or more. Then, having worshipped it according to the available ritual worship, one should present the offering (*bali*) with the root mantra accompanied by "Oṃ Guṃ Svāhā" and the *balimudrā*.

Then one should offer the *ali* (wine). The procedure for this is as follows: Having first performed the *kamalāvarta* (lotus-turning) gesture, one should visualize a lotus-vessel containing a lotus upon a lotus in the right hand; then, having raised the left vajra, with the mantra *oṃ haḥ hoḥ hrīḥ svāhā* preceded by the display of the *mahāmudrā*, one should take the yogic vessel (*yogapātra*) filled with *ali* in the right hand. Then, having meditated on a white letter *sa* in the palm of the left hand, surrounded by the sixteen vowels beginning with *a*, one should cover the vessel and behold the nectar (*amṛta*) as the *ali*. [2.3.123-125]

Thereafter, having made the thumb together with the syllable *hūṃ* into the earth, and having meditated upon Meru as being nameless and joined with the syllable *hūṃ*, one should perform the churning. Having visualized a stūpa at the throat, one should apply the *cchiḍiṅga* three times. Having thus applied it three times to body, speech, and mind, and having applied the *cchiḍiṅga* three times to all the yoginīs—[having seen and purified the Dharma, one must not abandon its realization].
Having recited, "The Brahmin, the dog, and the Caṇḍāla are of one and the same nature" (2.3.135),
one should offer it with the mantra: *oṃ haḥ hoḥ hrīḥ svāhā*.

Oṃ bhakṣa 3 sarvayogeśvari hūṃ 3 jaṃ svāhā. [2.3.158] Having formed two vajra-fists and joined them back-to-back, and having linked the two ring fingers and the two little fingers like a chain, one should cause [the disciple] to receive [the substances] preceded by the words "Balāt" and so forth. After offering the full range of worship and praising [the deity], one should say, "As you please. [cf. 2.3.140]
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by nature; I am pure by nature.
All phenomena are pure like a vajra; I am pure like a vajra.
All phenomena are pure through yoga; I am pure through yoga. Thus it is said.
Placing the vajra-añjali at the heart, one should recite.

Then, outside the mandala, one should visualize the deities in the eight directions within five groups of five situated upon a red triangular mandala. They are seated upon corpses, possessing the colors of the five ḍākinīs, and holding tridents and skull-cups. One should visualize Kṛṣṇarudra and the others, as well as Cāmuṇḍī and the rest, with skull-cups in their left hands.

Having formed two vajra-fists, one should join them back-to-back; having linked the two little fingers like a chain, one should release the two index fingers and, bending the right index finger, summon [the deity] with this: *oṃ kuru 2 samayādhipati hūṃ jaḥ svāhā*. One should worship with the offering of the wheel (*cakra-upacāra*), with the twenty-fold worship, and with the song of the syllable *hūṃ*.

Having placed Lāsyā between five lotuses, Vīṇā, Vaṃśā, Hāsā, Vādyā, Paṭahā, Maujyā, Tālā, Nṛtyā, and Vyajanā— having dismissed them with these, one should then perform the previously mentioned ritual procedure for the offering (bali) and the maṇḍala circle, and present the bali with all the mudrās and mantras as prescribed.

*Oṃ kuru 2 mahābaliṃ hūṃ svāhā.* At the time of the fire offering (*homa*), having extended both hands and moved the two middle thumbs, this is the *bali-mantra-mudrā*. At the time of the fire offering for the consumer of oblations (*hutāśana*), one should examine the fire. If it indicates an ill omen, then [one should recite]: *vajrasūkṣma hūṃ svāhā*. In whichever place the ill omen occurs, one should offer clarified butter (*ghṛta*) one hundred and eight times with the *tantra*, preceded by three sprinklings (*paryukṣaṇa*) with water that pacifies calamities. Having performed the offering in this manner, the fire offering to the root deity should be performed according to the previously stated sequence.
Having drawn [the breath] in with the breath, having caused it to rest within one's own body, and having released it, one should rise; such is the procedure for the fire-oblation (homa).

Having performed the sacrificial ritual by spreading out a canopy and hanging various cloths from it, one should prepare a square mandala with white fragrant powder. Having smeared the central vessel with white substances and filled it with milk-water and fragrance, having adorned it with sprouts and the like, and having provided the [offerings of] flowers, leaves, images, and time-indicators, one should present them.

Having recited "HŪṂ SUṂ KṢUṂ YUṂ HŪṂ SMṚYŪṂ HMRYŪṂ YMRYŪṂ KṢMRYŪṂ" eight times each, beginning with the *praṇava* (OM) and ending with *svāhā*, one should place the eight jars in their respective locations.
Having placed a large vessel in the center and having performed the entire self-yoga according to the previously stated sequence, one should worship oneself and then begin the external rite.

With "Oṃ kamalābhe svāhā," one should display the hollowed palms in the shape of a lotus. By means of that, one should visualize a lotus in the central vessel, covered by a white parasol together with a lunar disc.

There, by means of the syllable *HŪṂ*, one should meditate upon Jñānaḍākinī, empowered by Vajrahūṃkāra. She has two arms, is white in color, and sits in the sattvaparyaṅka posture. One should visualize her holding a vajra and a staff in her left and right hands respectively. To her east is Vajrī; to the north, Ghorī; to the west, Vetālī; and to the south, Caṇḍālī. In the northeast is Siṃhinī; in the southeast, Vyāghrī; in the southwest, Jambukī; and in the northwest, Ulūkī. They are to be visualized with the same emblems and ornaments as previously described.

The pledge (*samaya*) should be performed with the mudrā and mantra as previously stated: *oṃ samaye tiṣṭha hūṃ phaṭ*. Having formed the *vajrabandha*, extending the two index fingers, drawing them back, and forming a knot, one should display the pledge. One should worship as before: *oṃ hūṃ svāhā*. Having formed two *vajramuṣṭis*, one should place the left at the heart and the right above; this is the root mudrā-mantra.

Regarding the root mantra here: having offered water that impels according to one's desire, and having joined together *dūrvā* sprouts with *kunda* and other flowers, one should strike the crown-vajra of the Goddess while reciting the mantra once for each, endowed with meditative visualization (*bhāvanā*). One should perform the fire-oblation (*homa*) with *dūrvā* ten thousand times prior to this. Thus, there is the attainment of whatever is desired, as well as the increase of longevity and health. At the conclusion of the *homa*, one should present the sacrificial offering (*bali*) according to the prescribed instructions.

In all ritual actions, for the rite of pacification (*śāntika*), the white procedure is prescribed; facing east, one should utter the injunction: "Perform pacification! Remove all calamities! and so forth. With a rosary of one hundred beads held by the index finger, and with a peaceful mind, one should perform the pacification.

And for the rite of enrichment (*pauṣṭika*), with the yellow auxiliary [procedure] on all sides, facing north, one should say: "Perform enrichment! Summon all prosperity! and so forth. With a rosary of one hundred and eight beads held by the middle finger, and with a joyful mind, one should perform the enrichment.

For the purpose of subjugation (*vaśya*), with all red-colored offerings, one should place the twenty-syllable rosary on the ring finger and, with a deeply impassioned mind, perform the recitation while uttering the injunctions such as, "Bring [the person] facing west under control," "Draw [the enemy] toward me," and so forth.

And in the case of malevolent rites (*abhicāra*), one should perform the entire procedure in a single session, facing the southern direction, while uttering the injunctions such as "Kill! or "Expel! and so forth; with a mind possessed by wrath, one should carry out the malevolent rite using a rosary of sixty beads held by a maiden.
In brief, the procedures for the bali, homa, and yāga rites have been written according to the tradition of the Śrī Catuṣpīṭha Tantra.
